designs.design_notes: (MIL-HDBK-141 ch15) Worked design problem: 10X, 30 deg apparent half field, 5 mm exit pupil, eye relief at least 20 mm, line of sight displaced by Porro prisms. Erfle eyepiece chosen for the 30 deg field; its eye relief (about 0.8 f) sets the eyepiece focal length at 2.5 cm minimum, hence a 25 cm, f/5 objective. Prisms in 573574 glass, sized from a tunnel diagram allowing 50% vignetting at the field edge. Correction strategy: correct astigmatism and lateral color in the eyepiece (by cemented-surface curves or glass choice; reduced-dispersion positives make lateral color more positive), then correct axial color, spherical and coma of the whole system in the objective. Astigmatism near the edge is dominated by higher orders, so every change must be ray traced. Distortion follows from the astigmatism choice and is not objectionable in a viewing telescope. "Corrected by an expert designer": T and S split 3.7 D at the edge, mid-focus 0.8 D inside paraxial, essentially astigmatism-free to 20 deg if refocused.
not_verifiable: vignetting: 141 allows 50% at the field edge but gives no clear apertures; none are modeled
ray fan curves (Figs 15.4, 15.5): plotted only, beyond the printed F-C callouts
MTF, OPD, spot size: not given; computed in angular units via an ideal f = 1000 mm lens at the exit pupil

designs.design_notes: A Tessar whose front positive is split into two weaker positives. Splitting the most strongly bent element is the classic aperture-raising move: each half carries half the power at lower bending, so spherical aberration drops roughly fourfold for that element. Keeps the Tessar's rear cemented doublet and stop position.

designs.design_notes: The Tessar is a Cooke triplet whose rear positive is replaced by a cemented doublet (+ | - | stop | -+). The cemented interface adds a color-and-spherical control surface without another air space, which lets the 4-element lens reach f/2.8 to f/3.5 with a sharper center than the triplet. Compact and cheap, it was the default normal lens for half a century; its limits are corner astigmatism and zonal spherical beyond f/2.8.

designs.title: Schneider Super-Angulon 8/90 (symmetric wide angle 6/4), DE 975,637 Example 1

form.stop: center, between the two cemented doublets

source.ref: DE 975,637 (G. Klemt, Schneider Kreuznach, filed 1954), Example 1
source.locator: prescription file prepared by Bill Claff (photonstophotos.net), posted on lens-designs.com: DE00975637_Example01P.zmx

designs.design_notes: A near-symmetric wide angle for large format: strong negative outer menisci around two positive cemented doublets. The negative outer elements bend the oblique beams toward the axis, which keeps the illumination falloff and the Petzval sum down (the sum is near zero here), and the symmetry about the stop removes distortion, coma and lateral color. Covers about +/-50 deg at f/8; the long, heavy outer elements are its cost.
